'''Walter L. Sharpe III''' (born July 18, 1986) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Yulon (basketball)|Yulon]] of the [[Super Basketball League]] (SBL).

==Early career==
Sharpe attended Parker High School in [[Birmingham, Alabama]].

Considered a four-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Sharpe was listed as the No. 9 power forward and the No. 44 player in the nation in 2004.<ref>[https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Walter-Sharpe-12918 Walter Sharpe Recruiting Profile]</ref>

He later signed with [[Mississippi State University]]. Sharpe's career at Mississippi State was suspended frequently during his freshman season, declared academically ineligible during his sophomore season and eventually left the team.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/news/story?id=2296473 Mississippi State dismisses forwards Sharpe, Houston]</ref>

He transferred to the [[University of Alabama at Birmingham]], where he averaged 14.2 points per game in 12 games before being declared academically ineligible for the spring semester of the 2007–08 season.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://blog.al.com/spotnews/2008/01/uabs_walter_sharpe_is_academic.html|work=al.com|publisher=The Birmingham News|last=Irvine|first=Steve|date=January 15, 2008|title=UAB's Walter Sharpe is academically ineligible|access-date=March 20, 2013}}</ref>

==Professional career==
He was selected as the 32nd overall pick by the [[Seattle SuperSonics]] in the [[2008 NBA draft]]. Shortly after being drafted, the Sonics traded his rights to the [[Detroit Pistons]]. Shortly after being drafted, Sharpe was diagnosed with [[narcolepsy]], a sleeping disorder that causes excessive sleepiness.<ref name=yahoo/><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1817&dat=20080628&id=MssyAAAAIBAJ&sjid=Mb8EAAAAIBAJ&pg=6756,3759388|title = The Tuscaloosa News - Google News Archive Search}}</ref>

On July 13, 2009, he was traded along with [[Arron Afflalo]] to the [[Denver Nuggets]] for a second-round pick in the [[2011 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/afflalo_sharpe_trade_071309.html |title=Nuggets Acquire Afflalo, Sharpe from Detroit |work=NBA.com |date=July 13, 2009 |access-date=April 9, 2023}}</ref>

On July 31, 2009, he was traded along with [[Sonny Weems]] and cash considerations to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] for [[Malik Allen]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=4656 |title=Milwaukee Bucks trade Malik Allen to Denver Nuggets for Walter Sharpe, Sonny Weems and cash |work=InsideHoops.com |date=July 31, 2009 |access-date=March 19, 2013}}</ref> On October 26, 2009, he was waived by the Bucks.<ref>{{cite news|title=Walter Sharpe Waived By Bucks|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/199677/Walter-Sharpe-Waived-By-Bucks|access-date=March 12, 2015|work=realgm.com|date=October 26, 2009}}</ref>

On December 9, 2011, Sharpe signed with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] for the lockout-shortened 2011–12 season's training camp. On December 23, two days before the start of the regular season, Sharpe was waived by the Grizzlies.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/player/Walter-Sharpe/Summary/805|title = Walter Sharpe Player Profile, Memphis Grizzlies, NBA Stats, NCAA Stats, G League Stats, International Stats, Game Logs, Bests, Awards - RealGM}}</ref>

In March 2013, he signed with [[GlobalPort Batang Pier]] of the [[Philippine Basketball Association|PBA]], replacing [[Justin Williams (basketball)|Justin Williams]] as their import.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.court-side.com/news/blog/walter-sharpe-moves-to-global-port/ |title=Walter Sharpe moves to Global Port |access-date=March 13, 2013 |archive-date=March 21, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130321063136/http://www.court-side.com/news/blog/walter-sharpe-moves-to-global-port/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> On March 19, 2013, GlobalPort Batang Pier terminated his contract due to "conduct unbecoming of a professional basketball player" after a controversial photo of him sleeping on parking lot pavement went viral. GlobalPort Batang Pier team manager BJ Manalo said that they "will not tolerate actions of any local or foreign player who destroys the integrity" of both their team and that of the PBA. Sharpe played only two games in the PBA.<ref name=yahoo>[http://ph.sports.yahoo.com/news/nba--globalport-gives-sleeping-import-sharpe-the-boot-083136093.html GlobalPort gives sleeping import Sharpe the boot]</ref>

On July 1, 2014, he signed with [[Brujos de Guayama]] of Puerto Rico.<ref>{{cite news|title=Brujos de Guayama waive Mike Sweetney, sign Walter Sharpe|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/america/125271/brujos-de-guayama-waive-mike-sweetney-sign-walter-sharpe.html|access-date=March 12, 2015|work=Sportando.com|date=July 1, 2014}}</ref> He left Guayama after appearing in only one game.

On February 9, 2015, he signed with [[Cocodrilos de Caracas]] of Venezuela for the 2015 [[Superliga Profesional de Baloncesto|LPB]] season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Walter Sharpe es el tercer importado de Cocodrilos de Caracas|url=http://www.ultimasnoticias.com.ve/noticias/deportes/baloncesto/walter-sharpe-es-el-tercer-importado-de-cocodrilos.aspx|access-date=March 12, 2015|work=ultimasnoticias.com.ve|date=February 9, 2015|language=es}}</ref>
